general_ethiopia.best_time_to_visit: October to March (dry season) offers warm, sunny days ideal for travel. July–August is rainy season in most regions.
general_ethiopia.currency: Ethiopian Birr (ETB). Carry cash — card acceptance outside major hotels is limited.
general_ethiopia.tipping: 10% service charge is often included at hotels. Additional tipping of 50–100 ETB for good service is appreciated.
general_ethiopia.ethiopian_time: Ethiopians often use a 12-hour clock starting at dawn (6:00 AM international = 12:00 Ethiopian). Clarify AM/PM if scheduling.
general_ethiopia.language: Amharic is the national language. English is widely spoken in hotels and tourist areas. Learning 'Ameseginalehu' (thank you) and 'Selam' (hello) is appreciated.
health: Drink bottled or boiled water outside the hotel
Altitude: Addis Ababa is at 2,355m — allow a day to acclimatize if arriving from sea level
Malaria precautions recommended for lowland areas (Arba Minch, Omo Valley)
dress_code: Modest dress recommended at churches and religious sites (cover shoulders and knees)
Remove shoes when entering Ethiopian Orthodox churches
Resort casual wear is fine at Haile properties
photography: Always ask permission before photographing people
Some churches prohibit photography inside — look for signs or ask guides
general_ethiopia.connectivity: Ethiopian Telecom and Safaricom SIM cards available at the airport. Haile properties offer free Wi-Fi.

getting_there.from_addis_ababa: 275 km, 3.5–5 hours by car via the Addis–Hawassa highway. Selam Bus and other services run daily (5–6 hours). Direct flights to Hawassa Airport (~10 km from city).
getting_there.local_transport: Bajaj (tuk-tuk) is the easiest way around town. Agree on fare before boarding.

must_do: Boat ride on Lake Hawassa to spot hippos and birdlife (~500 ETB, ~1 hour)
Visit Amora Gedel fish market at sunrise — watch fishermen, pelicans, and fresh tilapia grilled on the spot
Hike Mount Tabor for panoramic views of the city and lake
Day trip to Wondo Genet hot springs (20 km away)
hawassa.best_season: Year-round destination. October–March is driest. Sidama New Year (Fiche Chembelala) is a unique cultural festival.
local_specialties: Sidama coffee — some of Ethiopia's finest
Avocado and mango from the Rift Valley
safety_tips: Do not swim in Lake Hawassa — hippos and bilharzia risk
Keep valuables secure at the fish market
packing: Light layers (evenings can be cool at 1,685m)

getting_there.from_addis_ababa: ~505 km, 7–8 hours by road. Ethiopian Airlines flies to Arba Minch Airport (free hotel shuttle).
getting_there.local_transport: Hotel can arrange tours. Bajaj available in town.

must_do: Boat trip on Lake Chamo to see crocodiles and hippos
Visit the 'Forty Springs' (Arba Minch means 'forty springs')
Nechisar National Park — zebras, gazelles, and diverse birdlife
Day trip to Dorze village for traditional bamboo houses and weaving
God's Bridge — natural rock arch between lakes Abaya and Chamo
arba minch.best_season: October–March. Gateway to Omo Valley tribal tours (multi-day trips).
local_specialties: Fresh fish from Lakes Abaya and Chamo
safety_tips: Respect cultural customs when visiting Omo Valley tribes — use licensed guides
Do not approach wild crocodiles outside guided tours
Carry insect repellent for lowland areas

getting_there.from_addis_ababa: ~160 km, 2.5–3 hours. Convenient stopover on the road to Hawassa or Bale Mountains.
getting_there.local_transport: Walking along the lakeside promenade. Bajaj for town trips.

must_do: Boat trip on Lake Ziway to see pelicans, fish eagles, and island monasteries
Birdwatching — over 200 species recorded
Visit Tulu Gudo island monastery (requires boat)
ziway.best_season: October–March for birdwatching. Lake levels vary seasonally.
local_specialties: Local wine from Ziway area vineyards
safety_tips: Book boat trips through the hotel concierge for safety

getting_there.from_addis_ababa: ~100 km, 1.5–2 hours via expressway. Popular weekend escape from the capital.

must_do: Explore Adama's markets and Rift Valley scenery
Day trip to nearby Awash National Park (wildlife, hot springs)
Visit Sodere hot springs resort area
adama.best_season: Year-round. Hotter than Addis due to lower elevation (~1,700m).
safety_tips: Stay hydrated — warmer and drier than highland cities
Use hotel transport for park visits
packing: Swimwear for hot springs day trips

getting_there.from_airport: Bole International Airport is 4.3 mi (7 km) away. Free hotel shuttle available — book in advance.
getting_there.local_transport: Ride apps (Ride, Feres) and blue taxis. Hotel concierge can arrange drivers.

must_do: National Museum — see 'Lucy', the 3.2-million-year-old hominid fossil
Holy Trinity Cathedral — burial site of Emperor Haile Selassie
Entoto Hill — panoramic city views and Maryam Church
Merkato — one of Africa's largest open-air markets
Addis Ababa Museum and Science Museum
Traditional coffee ceremony at a local coffee house
addis_ababa.best_season: October–May (dry season). Timkat (Epiphany, January) and Meskel (September) are spectacular festivals.
local_specialties: Injera with assorted wats at traditional restaurants
Tej (honey wine) at tej bet (wine houses)
safety_tips: Use registered taxis or ride apps at night
Keep valuables out of sight at Merkato

getting_there.from_addis_ababa: 730 km, ~12 hours by road or 1-hour flight to Gondar Airport.
getting_there.from_bahir_dar: 175 km, 3–4 hours. From Simien Mountains: 120 km.
getting_there.local_transport: Bajaj and taxis. Hotel arranges guided tours.

must_do: Fasil Ghebbi (Royal Enclosure) — UNESCO site with six castles from the 17th century
Debre Berhan Selassie Church — famous angel ceiling paintings
Fasilides' Bath — used for Timkat (Epiphany) celebrations
Simien Mountains National Park day trip or overnight (UNESCO, gelada baboons, dramatic scenery)
Kidame Gebeya market for local crafts
gondar.best_season: October–March. Timkat (January 19) is the most spectacular festival in Gondar.
safety_tips: Simien Mountains require warm clothing — temperatures drop significantly
Hire licensed guides for mountain treks
Respect church customs — women cover hair with shawl

cultural_etiquette.greetings: Handshakes are common. Ethiopians may touch shoulders during greeting among friends. 'Tenaystilign' (Amharic) or 'Nagaa' (Oromiffa) for hello.
cultural_etiquette.dining: Injera is both plate and utensil — tear off pieces to scoop food. Wash hands before and after eating. Guests are often served first.
cultural_etiquette.coffee_ceremony: It is polite to accept at least one cup. The third round (baraka) is considered a blessing.
cultural_etiquette.religious_sites: Women cover hair in Orthodox churches. Silence and respect are expected. No flash photography where prohibited.
